mechanism_narrative: A rising month-over-month Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals increasing inflationary pressure, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises month-over-month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% indicates a tight labor market that typically precedes wage inflation and Federal Reserve rate hikes, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE falls below 4.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and acceleration in employment growth (PAYEMS) indicates a rapidly tightening labor market, which often precedes inflationary pressures and Federal Reserve rate hikes, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in < 40% of instances when UNRATE declines and PAYEMS accelerates, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (as indicated by rising FEDFUNDS), the Federal Reserve's policy rate hikes compress equity valuations through higher discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 40% of instances during monetary tightening cycles, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) relative to its 12-month average indicates robust consumer demand and economic expansion, supporting positive equity valuations and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in < 40% of instances when HOUST is high, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 95.0 (index, 2017=100) signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in < 40% of instances when INDPRO falls below 95.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand and economic momentum, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in < 40% of instances when HOUST and RSAFS both rise, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion (as indicated by high quarterly GDP growth from GDPC1), the economy is nearing its peak, increasing recession risk and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in < 40% of instances during late-cycle expansions, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
